topics.label: Lecture framing and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening establishes the lecture’s scope, its relationship to previous teaching and the framework used to explain cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Signaling mutations that deregulate growth and survival
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular signaling pathways make cancer cells proliferate and survive independently of normal regulatory signals.

topics.label: Disrupted differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how altered differentiation produces abnormal cancer cell populations in hematological and intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how disruption of the p53–Bax–BCL2 balance enables cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Telomere maintenance and replicative immortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening limits cellular proliferation and how increased telomerase expression allows cancer cells to overcome that limit.

topics.label: p53-mediated genome protection and growth-control recap
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of growth control by explaining p53’s protective responses to cellular stress and recapping how mutations undermine normal growth constraints.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer-associated metabolic changes arise and contribute to tumor behavior.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how the angiogenic switch supplies the perfusion needed for tumor growth.

topics.label: Metastatic dissemination and establishment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what enables tumor cells to leave their primary site and establish clinically detectable tumors elsewhere.

topics.label: Closing synthesis and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the lecture’s overall message and learning goals before offering further reading and inviting questions.
